title: Validate caller control of owner_id BEFORE the insert in bandsintown/connect, because that is the only point at which an unvalidated owner_id enters event_provider_connections and every later reader inherits it
summary: DB-022 decided, with executed evidence, that the owning-account check for public.event_provider_connections CANNOT be expressed at the data boundary today, and therefore REMAINS PURELY APPLICATION-SIDE, with app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts named as the SINGLE consumer responsible for enforcing it (see the decision text proposed in DB-022.json under proposed_decisions; the orchestrator appends it to DECISIONS.md). This handoff discharges that half: the route is the only writer of owner_id, it validates nothing, and it is outside the database lane's grant, so it is routed rather than edited. The three READERS of the table already apply the created_by bound, measured rather than assumed: bandsintown/status:19 (.eq('created_by', user.id), plus the RLS read policy on its caller-side client), bandsintown/disconnect:32 (an explicit 403 on created_by !== user.id), and events/[id]/claim:73 (.eq('created_by', user.id), added by EVENTS-004). The single gap is the INGRESS. Measured on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with the chain's own statements extracted by line range: a service_role insert of a row naming an owner_id the creator does not control SUCCEEDS, because service_role carries BYPASSRLS and the four own-row policies are not on the writer's path. With an `authenticated` INSERT grant issued out of band it also SUCCEEDS, because the insert policy's WITH CHECK is `auth.uid() = created_by` and never mentions owner_id. That is the escalation primitive 20260927140000_event_provider_connections.sql:285-289 already names in its own comment. What the route must do is stated as a requirement, not as a patch: before the upsert, prove the caller controls (owner_type, owner_id) using the SAME account-resolution the domain already owns, and answer 403 on failure.
why_this_lane_cannot_close_it: Two reasons, both structural rather than matters of preference. (1) Grant: app/api/integrations/** is outside DB-022's working_set and outside this lane's charter; the record's scope.out names this route explicitly. (2) Substance: what `owner_id` IS for a given owner_type is not stated anywhere in the chain, the archive, or any of the five consumers, and the candidate references are not one-per-owner_type. Measured: the schema accepts a venue_profiles.id, a venues_v2.id AND an organizations.id under the same owner_type='venue' with zero refusals, because 20260823010000_venue_identity_bridge.sql declares a canonical identity TRIANGLE binding those three as three DISTINCT mirrors of one account. Two defensible current-control resolvers, both implementable from the active chain, return DIFFERENT SETS for the same rows (A = {venue_profiles, venues_v2}; B = {venues_v2, organizations} via the bridge). The organization arm disagrees the same way: is control `organizations.created_by`, or that plus `org_members` role in ('owner','admin')? The chain has both and picks neither for this table. So the database lane cannot write the predicate without first inventing the identity convention for a column whose convention the repository has never stated -- which is exactly what the read-only migration's own comment forbids at :221-224 ('a schema-level owner check here would be invented authorization for a relation whose contract this file does not own'). The one chain precedent for the identical problem, 20260825010000_ticketing_owner_account_resolution.sql, had to build a 100-line resolver for a DIFFERENT column and its own header records the defect it fixed: 'ownership only worked when the owner id happened to be a human auth user id'. Its venue arm is EVENT-SCOPED -- it reaches venue_profiles through events_v2.settings->>'venue_profile_id' or venue_identity_bridges -- and a provider connection has no event, so it cannot be lifted here even if the convention were settled.

blockers.title: bandsintown/connect inserts owner_type and owner_id straight from the request body
blockers.severity: authorization; latent, because the route is permanently 503 behind the disabled `external_event_providers` capability (lib/config/launch-capabilities.ts). It is the NEXT failure when that capability is enabled, and it is also the origin of the value events/[id]/claim now refuses to trust.
blockers.evidence: READ: app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts:36-54 -- `const input = connectSchema.parse(await request.json())` then `service.from('event_provider_connections').upsert({ owner_type: input.ownerType, owner_id: input.ownerId, ..., created_by: user.id }, { onConflict: 'owner_type,owner_id,provider,external_identity' })`. `connectSchema` is `z.object({ ownerType: z.enum(['artist','venue','organization']), ownerId: z.string().uuid(), externalIdentity, displayName })` (:8-13): the ownerId is validated as a UUID and for nothing else. The only auth is `getUser()` at :30-34. There is no call between the parse and the upsert that resolves the account or checks the caller against it.
blockers.measured_on_a_throwaway_instance: EXECUTED against PostgreSQL 16 with the chain's own create table, four policies and grants extracted by line range from supabase/migrations/20260927140000_event_provider_connections.sql, and a minimal auth/roles bootstrap: a service_role insert of ('organization', <org U1 does not control>, 'bandsintown', 'svc-row', U2) SUCCEEDED and the row was readable. With `grant insert, update on ... to authenticated` issued out of band, an authenticated insert naming a STRANGER's owner_id ALSO SUCCEEDED, because the policy's WITH CHECK is `auth.uid() = created_by` only. The chain's grant is the only thing preventing the second case today; the policy is not.
blockers.requested_action: integrations, on INTG-008: before the upsert, resolve (ownerType, ownerId) to its authoritative controller set and answer 403 when the session user is not in it. Use the domain's own account-resolution rather than a new one -- the ticketing lane's public.resolve_event_ticketing_owner_user_ids (20260825010000) is the existing pattern, but note its venue arm is event-scoped and cannot be reused verbatim, so the venue case needs a decision from the venue/identity lanes about which relation a provider connection's owner_id names (see HF-DB-022-CONNECT-OWNER-VALIDATION's sibling note in DB-022.proposed_decisions). Whatever the resolution, record the convention IN THE ROUTE and assert it in a test, because the schema does not record it and this is the second time an unstated id convention has cost this area a real fix. Fail closed: an unresolved (owner_type, owner_id) must be 403, never a permissive default. Also keep `.eq('created_by', user.id)` on every read, which is what the claim route now does.
blockers.note_on_the_claim_route: app/api/events/[id]/claim/route.ts is NOT part of this request and must not be edited for it. EVENTS-004 already closed its path with `.eq('created_by', user.id)` at :73, and that fix is load-bearing (proved red when removed). Its residual limit is recorded, not repaired there: created_by is a CREATED-TIME proxy, so a connection made while a user legitimately held the account keeps reading as theirs after they lose it, and a user who NOW controls the account is refused it. DB-022's contract asserts that limit rather than implying current control.

completed: Discharged HF-EVENTS-004-PROVIDER-OWNERSHIP-TO-DATABASE: the decision is recorded, evidence-backed, with the three decision facts turned into contract assertions rather than prose.

Measured, not assumed, that the four own-row policies constrain created_by only and that owner_id is unconstrained -- in both the read and the update direction, and with the grant issued so the POLICY is the thing under test.

Measured the created-time limit of created_by in BOTH directions: a caller who lost control still reads and updates the connection, and a caller who now holds control is refused it. No expiry column exists, so the proxy never decays.

Measured that the control relations DO exist in the active chain, which refutes the tempting 'the control relation is missing' answer, and then measured that the real obstacle is the unstated id convention, by building two resolvers that disagree.
Discharged DB-022's AC-5 by raising this handoff instead of widening the grant.
next_steps: integrations: implement the pre-insert owner control check in app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts, with a test that goes red when the check is removed.

integrations + venue: settle and record which relation owner_id names for owner_type='venue' (venue_profiles.id, venues_v2.id, or organizations.id via the identity triangle), and for owner_type='artist' whether a bare auth.users.id is admissible. This is a product-identity decision the database lane deliberately did not make and the schema cannot make.

integrations: do NOT widen the route to trust owner_id from the request under any mode. connection_mode is 'artist_owned_key' or 'partner' (20260927140000 CHECK) and neither makes a caller-supplied owner_id trustworthy.

database: if the convention above is settled, the follow-on is a forward-only migration adding the verified reference plus a current-control predicate, and it must first re-derive DB-022's decision rather than inherit it. The contract in this handoff's working set will go red when that happens, on purpose, and its violation message says so.
database: none before then. No further database work is required for this item.
completion_condition: app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts proves the session user controls the (owner_type, owner_id) pair before the upsert, answers a non-disclosing 403 when they do not (and 403 rather than a permissive default when the pair cannot be resolved), names the id convention it resolved against in the route, and has a regression test that is observed to go red when the check is removed. The table-level decision is not revisited by this handoff: DB-022 has already decided the check stays application-side.
verification: bash supabase/tests/db022_provider_ownership.harness.sh — PASS, `checks: 377   failures: 0` / `DB-022 provider-connection ownership: ALL 377 CHECKS PASS`, exit 0, on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster in a temp dir on a unix socket, run TWICE with a byte-identical sequence of all 377 check names. Includes 11 negative controls each demonstrated failing and an anti-vacuity control for the violation counter itself.

INSTRUMENT VALIDATION, the reason the run above is evidence and not a claim: the same harness was run against two deliberately broken COPIES of the chain in a temp root, with the same instrument. (a) `event_provider_connections_owner_read` widened to `USING (true)`: the chain's own post-condition rejected the fixture and the run ABORTED at stage 1. (b) an `owner_id` FOREIGN KEY added in place, with no line shift so the extraction could not drift: the chain's own post-condition stayed SILENT, the db022 contract went red with exactly one violation carrying the DECISION DB-022 message, and 24 behavioural checks failed -- including that a service_role insert of a stranger's owner_id is then refused, and that the two disagreeing resolvers no longer disagree because the ambiguity is gone. So the decision this handoff carries is falsifiable by a future migration, and the instrument is shown to notice.

NOTHING WAS APPLIED TO ANY ENVIRONMENT. No `supabase db reset`, no forced or full-chain replay, no `migration up`, no `db push`, no targeted push (CP-051). No hosted, database, or advisory evidence is claimed or implied; a clean local replay is not a measurement of any deployed environment. The four policies' behaviour was measured on a LOCAL EMULATION of a Supabase-shaped target, not read off a live catalog.

NOT RUN AND NOT CLAIMED: npm run typecheck (CP-106: a full-repo typecheck OOMs on this machine by design; no TypeScript file was authored or modified by this task, so there was nothing to scope). npm run generate:database-types and npm run check:database-types (both need an applied target, and DB-008's backward-drift finding on public.venue_profiles still blocks a chain-only regeneration). supabase db lint --local (no running target). No handoff-receiving task record for INTG-008 was created here; that is the orchestrator's dispatch, and this handoff carries `accepting_task_id: INTG-008` with `status: pending` until it is accepted.
not_claimed: This handoff asserts what the WRITTEN chain specifies and what that shape does on a local emulation. It does not assert the state of any deployed environment: whether 20260927140000 has been applied anywhere, whether the live policy set matches it, and whether any live connection rows exist are all unverified here. The presence of a gap in the code is not the presence of an exploit in production, and the absence of a hosted finding is not evidence of safety.
